title: Injection
description: Flaws occurring when untrusted user input is concatenated into interpreters (SQL, OS commands, templates, parsers, serializers) and executed as native code.

attacks.name: SQL injection — error-based
attacks.desc: Forcing database syntax errors (e.g. via CONVERT, CAST, or extractvalue) that reflect query results or internal database error messages directly in the HTTP response.
attacks.prevention: Use parameterized SQL queries; do not concatenate untrusted values into query strings, even when errors are hidden.

attacks.name: SQL injection — union-based
attacks.desc: Appending UNION SELECT operators to vulnerable queries to combine results from targeted system tables into the original query result set rendered on screen.
attacks.prevention: Bind query values with prepared statements and allowlist any dynamic identifiers such as sort columns.

attacks.name: SQL injection — boolean blind
attacks.desc: Inferring database contents character by character by injecting true/false SQL conditions and observing subtle application behavior differences (content changes, missing elements).
attacks.prevention: Use prepared statements for every query branch; blind responses still reveal unsafe string interpolation.

attacks.name: SQL injection — time-based blind
attacks.desc: Extracting information by injecting conditional sleep statements (e.g. WAITFOR DELAY, pg_sleep()) and measuring the exact server response delay to deduce data bits.
attacks.prevention: Parameterize queries and set sensible timeouts; suppressing error output does not fix timing-based injection.

attacks.name: SQL injection — out-of-band
attacks.desc: Coercing the database server to perform outbound DNS lookups or SMB connections containing extracted data payloads (e.g. utl_http, master..xp_dirtree).
attacks.prevention: Bind values and limit database network egress so an injection cannot invoke external lookup channels.

attacks.name: SQL injection — second order
attacks.desc: Storing an injection payload safely into the database during an initial transaction, which is later retrieved and concatenated unsafely into a secondary SQL query.
attacks.prevention: Parameterize both the original write and any later query that consumes stored user-controlled data.

attacks.name: NoSQL injection
attacks.desc: Injecting NoSQL query operators (such as $ne, $gt, $regex) via JSON payloads or parsed parameters to alter document queries and bypass authentication.
attacks.prevention: Use driver-supported structured query builders, validate value types, and reject operator keys from untrusted objects.

attacks.name: ORM injection
attacks.desc: Exploiting unsafe parameter concatenation or vulnerable methods inside Object-Relational Mapping layers to alter database query logic.
attacks.prevention: Use ORM parameter binding and safe query APIs; do not splice untrusted fragments into raw query methods.

attacks.name: Command injection
attacks.desc: Injecting shell command separators (e.g. ;, &&, |, `) into parameters passed to operating system command execution functions to execute arbitrary shell commands.
attacks.prevention: Avoid shell invocation when a direct API exists; otherwise pass fixed executables and validated arguments without a shell.

attacks.name: Blind command injection
attacks.desc: Executing operating system commands without visible stdout/stderr in responses, confirming execution via time delays (sleep) or out-of-band interactions.
attacks.prevention: Use the same safe process APIs for background jobs, and monitor executions without assuming lack of output means safety.

attacks.name: Argument injection
attacks.desc: Passing crafted input into command-line utilities (e.g. curl, tar, git, sendmail) that get interpreted as command flags (e.g. -o, --output, --upload-file) to alter utility behavior.
attacks.prevention: Separate program options from untrusted values with supported argument terminators and allowlist accepted parameters.

attacks.name: LDAP injection
attacks.desc: Injecting LDAP filter syntax characters to manipulate directory search queries, enabling unauthorized user enumeration and privilege validation.
attacks.prevention: Use safe LDAP filter builders or escape according to the exact LDAP context, rather than concatenating input.

attacks.name: XPath injection
attacks.desc: Manipulating XPath queries used to search XML documents, bypassing authentication or retrieving hidden data nodes via logical expression injection.
attacks.prevention: Use parameterized XPath expressions where supported and avoid building XPath syntax from raw strings.

attacks.name: SSTI — Jinja2
attacks.desc: Injecting template syntax into Jinja2 templates (e.g. {{config.items()}} or python MRO traversal) to escape the sandbox and execute arbitrary system commands.
attacks.prevention: Pass user content as template data, never as a Jinja2 template source; restrict template authoring to trusted code.

attacks.name: SSTI — Twig
attacks.desc: Exploiting template syntax evaluation in PHP Twig engines to execute functions such as system() or exec() through built-in filter abuse.
attacks.prevention: Keep Twig templates trusted and pass untrusted text only as data with context-aware escaping.

attacks.name: SSTI — Freemarker / Velocity
attacks.desc: Injecting template tags into Apache FreeMarker or Velocity engines using built-in directives (e.g. ?api, ?new) to invoke Java classes and execute commands.
attacks.prevention: Prevent untrusted users from editing Freemarker or Velocity template source, and run templates with restricted capabilities.

attacks.name: Expression Language injection
attacks.desc: Injecting expressions into Spring SpEL, Apache Struts OGNL, or JSP EL to execute arbitrary Java methods within the server JVM runtime.
attacks.prevention: Avoid evaluating untrusted SpEL or OGNL expressions; use fixed expressions and typed parameters instead.

attacks.name: XXE — in-band
attacks.desc: Supplying custom XML external entity definitions in user-submitted XML documents, forcing the XML parser to read and return local system files in the response.
attacks.prevention: Disable external entities and DTDs in XML parsers, and use maintained parser settings for every XML entry point.

attacks.name: Blind XXE
attacks.desc: Exfiltrating file contents via out-of-band XML parameter entities when error messages and direct XML response echoes are suppressed.
attacks.prevention: Apply the same entity restrictions to parsers used in background and asynchronous flows, and restrict outbound network access.

attacks.name: XXE via file upload
attacks.desc: Embedding malicious XML external entity declarations inside uploaded document formats that are secretly ZIP archives of XML files (DOCX, XLSX) or vector images (SVG).

attacks.name: SSRF
attacks.desc: Coercing a backend web server into making unintended network requests to arbitrary internal or external addresses, bypassing firewall boundaries.

attacks.name: Blind SSRF
attacks.desc: Triggering server-side requests where the response content is not returned to the client, verified via out-of-band DNS/HTTP listener logs or timing differences.

attacks.name: SSRF via DNS rebinding
attacks.desc: Bypassing IP address validation filters by utilizing a custom DNS server that returns a public IP during initial check, but resolves to 127.0.0.1 immediately on subsequent lookup.

attacks.name: SSRF to cloud metadata
attacks.desc: Targeting cloud instance link-local metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) to harvest IAM temporary security credentials and machine tokens.

attacks.name: SSRF to internal services
attacks.desc: Pivoting through vulnerable web servers to probe and exploit non-public internal services (Redis, Consul, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes kubelet) running on loopback or private LANs.

attacks.name: CRLF injection
attacks.desc: Injecting \r\n sequences into user inputs reflected in HTTP response headers, allowing attackers to introduce arbitrary headers or inject HTML body content.

attacks.name: Header injection
attacks.desc: Injecting unwanted HTTP headers into outgoing backend requests or incoming responses to alter caching, proxy routing, or security controls.

attacks.name: Email header injection
attacks.desc: Inserting newline characters into web contact forms to inject CC, BCC, or Subject headers into backend mail systems, transforming the server into a spam relay.

attacks.name: Log injection / forging
attacks.desc: Injecting carriage returns and fake timestamp strings into logged inputs to corrupt audit trails, forge log events, or exploit vulnerable log parsing viewers.

attacks.name: Log4Shell / JNDI injection
attacks.desc: Exploiting recursive string lookup formatting in Apache Log4j to trigger JNDI lookups to LDAP/RMI servers, downloading and executing malicious Java bytecode.

attacks.name: CSV / formula injection
attacks.desc: Prefixing user input fields with =, +, -, or @ characters that execute dynamic DDE formulas or launch system applications when exported and opened in spreadsheet software.

attacks.name: HTTP Parameter Pollution
attacks.desc: Supplying duplicate parameter names (e.g. ?id=1&id=2) to exploit disparities between web servers and backend systems in parameter handling order to bypass WAF rules.

attacks.name: Java deserialization
attacks.desc: Submitting crafted serialized Java objects that trigger gadget chains (e.g. CommonsCollections, Spring) during readObject() deserialization, resulting in remote code execution.

attacks.name: PHP deserialization
attacks.desc: Passing malicious serialized strings to PHP unserialize(), invoking magic methods (__destruct, __wakeup, __toString) in application classes to execute arbitrary code.

attacks.name: Python pickle deserialization
attacks.desc: Supplying malicious Python pickle byte streams that implement __reduce__() to invoke os.system() or arbitrary callable functions during unpickling.

attacks.name: .NET ViewState deserialization
attacks.desc: Exploiting unencrypted or unvalidated ASP.NET __VIEWSTATE parameters with known validation keys to deserialize gadget chains (e.g. ActivitySurrogateSelector) for code execution.

attacks.name: Prototype pollution
attacks.desc: Injecting properties via __proto__, constructor, or prototype into recursive object merge/clone functions, polluting the global JavaScript Object prototype.

attacks.name: ReDoS
attacks.desc: Submitting crafted input strings to regular expressions with overlapping nested quantifiers, causing exponential backtracking that freezes the thread and CPU.

attacks.name: Insecure deserialization via cookies
attacks.desc: Tampering with serialized session objects stored in cookies (e.g. Python pickle or Ruby Marshal) to execute arbitrary commands when unpacked by the server.

attacks.name: SSI injection
attacks.desc: Injecting Server-Side Include directives (e.g. <!--#exec cmd="id" -->) into pages parsed by web servers with SSI enabled, resulting in command execution.

attacks.name: XSLT injection
attacks.desc: Injecting into or providing arbitrary XSLT stylesheets processed by servers, invoking extension functions (e.g. system-property, php:function) to execute code.

attacks.name: LFI
attacks.desc: Manipulating file inclusion parameters in languages like PHP (include/require) to load and execute local files or logs containing injected script code.

attacks.name: RFI
attacks.desc: Exploiting unvalidated file inclusion functions with allow_url_include enabled to load and execute scripts hosted on remote web servers.

attacks.name: PHP wrappers
attacks.desc: Utilizing built-in PHP I/O streams such as php://filter to read base64-encoded source code, or data:// to inject and execute inline PHP code.

attacks.name: Arbitrary file read
attacks.desc: Supplying file paths to download or file-viewing endpoints lacking path traversal sanitation, allowing unauthorized retrieval of system and configuration files.

attacks.name: Arbitrary file write
attacks.desc: Controlling the destination filename and contents in upload or file-saving handlers to overwrite critical server files (cron jobs, authorized_keys, webshells).

attacks.name: File upload bypass — extension
attacks.desc: Bypassing file extension blocklists using alternative executable extensions (.php5, .phtml, .phar), double extensions (.php.png), or null bytes (.php%00.jpg).

attacks.name: File upload bypass — MIME / magic bytes
attacks.desc: Bypassing server validation by spoofing the Content-Type request header or prepending legitimate file signature magic bytes (GIF89a) to executable webshells.

attacks.name: Zip slip
attacks.desc: Exploiting directory traversal filenames (../../shell.php) inside archive archives (ZIP, TAR) that write files outside target extraction directories during unpacking.

attacks.name: XML bomb / billion laughs
attacks.desc: Submitting XML documents with recursively defined entities that expand exponentially during parsing, causing memory exhaustion and process crashing.

attacks.name: JSON injection
attacks.desc: Injecting unescaped quotes and colons into concatenated JSON strings, modifying keys or altering payload structure sent to internal services.

attacks.name: YAML deserialization
attacks.desc: Exploiting unsafe YAML loaders (such as PyYAML yaml.load without SafeLoader) that instantiate arbitrary language objects and execute code on parse.

attacks.name: EL injection
attacks.desc: Injecting into Java Unified Expression Language (${...}) evaluations in web frameworks to invoke runtime system commands.

attacks.name: H2 / HSQLDB console RCE
attacks.desc: Accessing exposed embedded database web consoles (H2 Database) and creating stored aliases or triggering JNDI lookups in JDBC URLs to achieve code execution.
